title: Ordering and Sequencing
tagline: Year 2 — Ranking by comparisons, dictionary order, logical sequences and day problems

introduction.overview: Ordering questions give you a few comparisons (A is taller than B; C is lighter than D) and ask who is tallest, lightest or in the middle. Sequencing questions ask you to arrange words in dictionary order, in a logical order (stages of a process, units of size) or by the day of the week. The key skill is to combine the comparisons into one ordered line and to read the answer from it.
introduction.placementRelevance: Ordering and sequencing questions are commonly asked in company reasoning rounds. They are quick if you build the full line before answering.
introduction.realWorldContext: Ranking candidates, scheduling events, ordering steps in a process and calendar calculations use these methods.

learningObjectives: Combine several comparisons into a single ordered line
Identify the highest, lowest, nth and middle person
Arrange words in dictionary order and logical order
Detect when the information is insufficient

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: The seven days repeat every 7 days; dividing a number of days by 7 gives the remainder shift. Dictionary order compares letters left to right.

coreDefinitions: Order: the arrangement of items by a property such as height, age, weight or speed.
Transitivity: if A > B and B > C then A > C.
Dictionary (alphabetical) order: compare the first letters, then the second, and so on; a shorter word that is the start of a longer one comes first.
Logical sequence: arrangement by natural order of stages (seed, plant, flower, fruit) or size (village, district, state).
Odd days: remainder when the number of days is divided by 7.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: Each comparison is a link in a chain. Join the links wherever they share a person, and you get a single line. If two pieces cannot be joined, the order between them is undetermined.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Write the comparisons as symbols (A > B). Combine them into one line from highest to lowest. Then read off whichever position the question asks.

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Chaining comparisons
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: A > B and B > C ⇒ A > B > C

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Position in the line
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: nth from the top = (total − n + 1)th from the bottom

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Dictionary order
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Compare letter by letter; shorter prefix first

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Odd days
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Days later = number of days mod 7

importantRulesAndFormulas.title: Logical sequences
importantRulesAndFormulas.formula: Order by size, time or process

mainNarrative: Write each comparison as a symbol and chain them. A taller than B, C shorter than B but taller than D, and E the tallest gives E > A > B > C > D. The second tallest is A, the middle person is B.
If a piece does not connect, the order is not determined. If you know only A > B and C > D, you cannot compare A with C. A good question will always give enough links for the asked position.
For dictionary order, compare the first letters, then the second letters and so on. A shorter word that is the start of a longer word comes first. So Tab, Tabby, Table, Tablet is the correct order.

For days of the week, find the number of days between the dates, divide by 7 and add the remainder to the weekday. If 15 August is a Thursday, 26 August is 11 days later; 11 mod 7 = 4, and Thursday + 4 days is Monday. January has 31 days and February 28, so 1 March is 59 days after 1 January, a shift of 3 days.
For logical sequences, use the natural order: egg, larva, pupa, adult; village, district, state, country, continent. Decide whether the question asks for the order by size, time or process.

deepDiveAspects.title: Insufficient data
deepDiveAspects.content: If the comparisons do not link everything, the question may be unanswerable. In exams, the option "cannot be determined" is usually present for this case.

deepDiveAspects.title: Leap years
deepDiveAspects.content: In a leap year February has 29 days. A leap year has 366 days, which is 2 odd days.

solvedExamples.title: Chaining comparisons
solvedExamples.question: A is taller than B. C is shorter than B but taller than D. E is the tallest. Who is the second tallest?
solvedExamples.whyItWorks: E is first, so the second is the tallest of the rest.

solvedExamples.title: Dictionary order
solvedExamples.question: Arrange Cat, Cart, Car and Cab in dictionary order. Which comes last?

steps.title: Common start
steps.explanation: All start with C. Second letter a.

steps.title: Third letters
steps.explanation: b < r < r < t, so Cab first, then Car and Cart, and Cat last.

steps.title: Car vs Cart
steps.explanation: Car is a prefix of Cart, so Car comes first.

solvedExamples.title: Day of the week
solvedExamples.question: 1 January 2021 was a Friday. What day was 1 March 2021?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Write each statement as a > b, chain them into one line, and count positions.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Test options against every given comparison.

easy.question: A is taller than B, and B is taller than C. Who is the tallest?
easy.explanation: A > B > C, so A is the tallest.

easy.question: P is heavier than Q and R is lighter than Q. Who is the lightest?
easy.explanation: P > Q > R, so R is the lightest.

easy.question: Which of these words comes first in dictionary order: Table, Tablet, Tab, Tabby?
easy.explanation: Tab is a prefix of the others and comes first: Tab, Tabby, Table, Tablet.

intermediate.question: A is taller than B. C is shorter than B but taller than D. E is the tallest. The second tallest is
intermediate.explanation: E > A > B > C > D, so A is second.

intermediate.question: P is richer than Q, R is richer than P and S is poorer than Q. The second richest is
intermediate.explanation: R > P > Q > S, so P is second.

intermediate.question: Arrange Planet, Plane, Plant and Plain in dictionary order. The third word is
intermediate.explanation: Plain, Plane, Planet, Plant. The third is Planet.

advanced.question: A is faster than B, C is slower than D, B is faster than D and E is faster than A. The third fastest is
advanced.explanation: E > A > B > D > C. The third is B.

advanced.question: 1 January 2021 was a Friday. 1 March 2021 was a
advanced.explanation: Days between = 31 + 28 = 59, which leaves 3 when divided by 7. Friday + 3 = Monday.

placementStyle.explanation: P > Q > S > T > R. The second lightest is T.

placementStyle.question: Arranged in decreasing order of size: Village, District, State, Country, Continent. The third is
placementStyle.explanation: Continent > Country > State > District > Village. The third is State.
